periods.label: Creation & Flood
periods.description: The ancient world of biblical origins: Eden, Noah's flood and the dispersion of nations after Babel.

maps.title: The Garden of Eden — Traditional location
maps.caption: Tradition places Eden in Mesopotamia, at the confluence of the Tigris and Euphrates (Genesis 2:10-14).
maps.details: The 4 rivers of Eden: Pishon, Gihon, Hiddekel (Tiger) and Phrat (Euphrates)

maps.title: Noah's Ark — Mount Ararat
maps.caption: The Ark landed on the Ararat Mountains in what is now eastern Türkiye (Genesis 8:4).
maps.details: Mount Ararat peaks at 5,165 m, on the Turkish-Armenian border

maps.title: The Tower of Babel — Plain of Shinar
maps.caption: Babel (Babylon) is located on the plain of Shinar in Mesopotamia (Genesis 11:2).
maps.details: Archaeologists have discovered giant ziggurats in Babylon and Ur

periods.label: Patriarchs
periods.description: The journeys of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob through Canaan, Egypt and Mesopotamia.

maps.title: Abraham's Journey — From Ur to Canaan
maps.caption: Abraham departs from Ur of the Chaldeans, passes through Harran, goes down to Canaan and to Egypt (Genesis 11-12).
maps.details: A journey of more than 2,000 km from Mesopotamia to Canaan

maps.title: Canaan in the time of the Patriarchs
maps.caption: The holy places of the Patriarchs: Shechem, Bethel, Hebron, Beersheba — the Route of the Patriarchs.
maps.details: Abraham, Isaac and Jacob built altars along the length of Canaan

maps.title: Egypt in the time of Joseph
maps.caption: Joseph sold to Egypt becomes governor. The land of Goshen welcomes Jacob's family (Genesis 37-50).
maps.details: The Nile Delta and the Goshen region were inhabited by the Hebrews

periods.label: Exodus & Desert
periods.description: The exit from Egypt, the 40 years in the Sinai desert and the arrival at the gates of Canaan.

maps.title: The Road of Exodus — From Egypt to Sinai
maps.caption: The Israelites cross the Red Sea and enter the desert towards Mount Sinai (Exodus 14-19).
maps.details: Several Exodus routes are proposed: northern route, central or southern route

maps.title: Mount Sinai — Place of Revelation
maps.caption: Sinai (Jebel Musa or Horeb) is the place where Moses received the Ten Commandments (Exodus 19-20).
maps.details: The Sinai Peninsula is the scene of the 40 years of wandering of the Hebrew people

maps.title: 40 Years in the Desert — Stages
maps.caption: From Kadesh-Barnea to the plains of Moab, the stages of the people: Elim, Mara, Rephidim, Kadesh...
maps.details: Numbers 33 lists 40 steps from leaving Egypt to entering Canaan

periods.label: Conquest & Judges
periods.description: The crossing of the Jordan under Joshua, the distribution of the tribes and the period of the Judges.

maps.title: The Conquest of Canaan under Joshua
maps.caption: Joshua led 3 campaigns: central (Jericho, Ai), southern and northern to conquer Canaan (Joshua 1-12).
maps.details: The fall of Jericho opens the central campaign to conquer Canaan

maps.title: Distribution of the 12 Tribes of Israel
maps.caption: Each of the 12 tribes receives its territory. Levi does not receive territory but cities of refuge (Joshua 13-21).
maps.details: The tribes of Reuben, Gad and half-tribe of Manasseh settle east of the Jordan

maps.title: The Period of Judges — External Threats
maps.caption: Israel's enemies under the Judges: Philistines (west coast), Moabites (east), Midianites (south), Canaanites (north).
maps.details: The cycle of Judges: disobedience → oppression → repentance → deliverance → peace

periods.label: United Kingdom & Divided
periods.description: The reign of Saul, David and Solomon, then the division into the kingdoms of Israel and Judah.

maps.title: The United Kingdom under David and Solomon
maps.caption: David conquers Jerusalem and extends the kingdom from Egypt to the Euphrates. Solomon builds the Temple (1 Kings 4-8).
maps.details: Jerusalem, conquered from the Jebusites, becomes the political and religious capital

maps.title: Jerusalem — The City of David
maps.caption: David established his capital in Jerusalem (Zion) and brought the Ark of the Covenant there (2 Samuel 5-6).
maps.details: Mount Moriah hosts the Temple of Solomon, built in 7 years (966-959 BC)

maps.title: Kingdom Division—Israel and Judah
maps.caption: After Solomon: the North (Israel, 10 tribes, capital Samaria) and the South (Judah, 2 tribes, capital Jerusalem) (1 Kings 12).
maps.details: The Northern Kingdom will last 200 years (931-722 BC), the Kingdom of Judah 340 years (931-586 BC)

periods.label: Exile & Return
periods.description: The fall of Samaria (722), the destruction of Jerusalem (586), the exile to Babylon and the return under Cyrus.

maps.title: The Assyrian Deportation — 722 BC AD
maps.caption: Sargon II of Assyria deports the 10 northern tribes to Mesopotamia (2 Kings 17). The Samaritans will get involved.
maps.details: Foreign populations settled in Samaria, creating the mixed people of the Samaritans

maps.title: The Babylonian Empire and the Exile of Judah
maps.caption: Nebuchadnezzar destroys Jerusalem (586) and deports Judah's elite to Babylon. Daniel and Ezekiel prophesied there.
maps.details: 3 successive deportations: 605, 597 and 586 BC. J.C. Jeremiah remains in Judea

maps.title: Return from Exile — Cyrus' Decree
maps.caption: In 538 BC. BC, Cyrus the Great allows the Jews to return and rebuild the Temple (Ezra 1).
maps.details: Zerubbabel leads the 1st return (538), Ezra the 2nd (458), Nehemiah the 3rd (445 BC)

periods.label: New Testament times
periods.description: Palestine in the time of Jesus, Paul's missionary journeys and the spread of the Gospel.

maps.title: Palestine in the time of Jesus
maps.caption: Palestine is divided into Galilee, Samaria and Judea. Jesus was born in Bethlehem, grew up in Nazareth, preached in Galilee.
maps.details: Lake Tiberias (Sea of ​​Galilee) is the heart of Jesus' Galilean ministry

maps.title: Paul's Missionary Journeys
maps.caption: Paul completed 3 missionary journeys from Antioch, evangelizing Turkey, Greece and reaching Rome.
maps.details: 1st journey (Acts 13-14): Cyprus and Asia Minor. 2nd: Macedonia and Greece. 3rd: Ephesus

maps.title: The Roman Empire and the Spread of the Gospel
maps.caption: The Pax Romana, Roman roads and the common Greek language facilitated the spread of the Gospel.
maps.details: In less than 300 years, Christianity spread from Jerusalem to the ends of the Empire
